name: @iron-software/astro-components

props.name: variant
props.description: Figma `779:3486` ships `variant=subtle|solid`; this took a `solid` boolean until 2026-08-11. Eight components in this library express their variant axis as an enum named `variant` and Badge was the only one spelling one as a boolean — the same reasoning that turned `small` into `size` below.

props.name: size
props.description: Figma `779:3486` ships `size=sm|md`; this took a `small` boolean until 2026-08-06.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let a long label wrap instead of leaving the box. Off by default: a button is normally short and one line reads better. Turn it on where the label is long and the container is narrow — the Footer band is the case that found this, where "Get Full 10 products Suite" needs 309.5px against 248px of room at a 320 viewport and was being cut, silently, by an ancestor's `overflow: hidden`. This has to be a prop rather than a class passed in. `whitespace-nowrap` below and a `whitespace-normal` on the call site are both one class deep, so the winner is decided by their order in the compiled stylesheet, not by the order they are written — and Tailwind emits `normal` at 1111 and `nowrap` at 1114, so the override loses. `[white-space:normal]` lands in the same place and loses identically.

props.name: variant
props.description: Suite: full-brand headline for homepage/generic pages. Default: names the current product (cross-sell).

props.name: productName
props.description: Required when variant="default" — e.g. "IronPDF"

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Heading level for the band's headline. The band is a section of a page, not a page of its own, so it cannot know how deep it sits — pass the level that keeps the host page's outline unbroken. Default 2.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the band's landmark, read by the "list of regions" view.

props.name: donateImgSrc
props.description: Asset paths. These default to SITE-ROOT paths, not paths relative to the page: `assets/logo.svg` resolves against the current URL, so it is correct only on a page that happens to sit at `/` and 404s on `/pricing` — silently, because a missing image logs nothing a build can fail on. A consuming app that keeps these in `public/assets/` needs to pass nothing; anything else passes its own path. The docs are the one caller that must override, because they are published under a repository subpath.

props.name: rainbowSrc
props.description: The band's rainbow backdrop. It is a PROP and painted inline for a reason: as a bracketed `bg-` arbitrary value holding the url, the path was baked into the compiled stylesheet, where a consumer's bundler rewrote it to `/_astro/assets/Rainbow.svg` and it 404'd with the band rendering flat — and no prop existed to correct it, so the roi-calculator carried an `!important` global override instead of a value. The class is deliberately NOT spelled out above. Tailwind extracts candidates from the whole file, COMMENTS INCLUDED, so writing it compiles it straight back into every consumer's stylesheet — the exact bug this prop exists to remove. The band stopped wearing the class on 2026-08-18 (`ececa65`); the string survived in this comment until 2026-08-21, and every consumer build in between still printed `assets/Rainbow.svg … didn't resolve at build time`. Nothing here could see it: this repo's own pipeline strips comments before Tailwind reads them (`build-utilities.mjs`) and a consumer's does not. `check:prose-classes` fails if it comes back.

props.name: variant
props.description: Figma's variant axis, scoped to the kind: wordmark takes default/ondark/mono/onhero (`mono` and `onhero` are iron-only — suite has neither in Figma); lockup takes basic/stack. `onhero` is the colour mark beside an ALL-WHITE wordmark, added 2026-08-21 (Figma `Main logo` variant `Onhero`). It exists because `ondark` is not enough over PHOTOGRAPHY: it keeps SOFTWARE on `brand/primary`, which measures 1.21:1 against a warm image. That is not fixable by treating the image — the colour's luminance is 0.173, so it reaches only 4.46:1 against pure black and can never clear the 4.5 bar on any dark ground. `mono` solves it by discarding all four brand colours; `onhero` keeps them and whitens only the wordmark. Over `bg-dark-shade` use `ondark`: SOFTWARE clears 4.04:1 there, and the pink is the point. In Figma the wordmark is one TEXT bound to `text/on dark/heading` — the same variable IRON already used — rather than a raw white.

props.name: mono
props.description: kind="mark" only — swaps to the black knockout artwork.

props.name: size
props.description: kind="mark" / "element". The mark is drawn on an 8-unit grid in a 96-unit box, so the multiples of 24 keep the most edges on whole pixels. MEASURED 2026-08-21, because the rule had been stated but never counted; re-measured and widened to the full ladder 2026-08-24. Share of path coordinates landing on a whole pixel, across all the artwork this component ships: 24px 48px 56px 64px 72px 96px 144px 192px mark 11.4% 18.9% 3.4% 5.7% 11.4% 18.9% 18.9% 19.0% element 2.1% 4.2% 0.5% 2.8% 2.1% 12.6% 4.2% 12.6% THE LADDER IS EVERY MULTIPLE OF 24, and it is the same answer from two directions. Arithmetically: the artwork is drawn on 8-unit coordinates in a 96-unit box, so a coordinate 8k lands whole at size S when kS/12 is an integer, which for every k means S divisible by 12 — and the second tier, the coordinates on 4-unit steps, needs 24. The table agrees: 24/48/72/96/ 144/192 measure 11.4-19.0% and NOTHING else clears 6.7%. Conventionally: the near-universal icon ladder is the 8-point grid (Material's baseline icon is 24 and its largest standard is 48; Tailwind's `size-*` runs 16/20/24/32/40/48/64/80/96). Multiples of 24 are exactly where the industry ladder and this artwork's own arithmetic agree, so the union is that. CONFIRMED AGAINST THE RENDER, not just the path data. Coordinates are a proxy; what a reader sees is pixels. Six marks were rasterised at nineteen sizes and the pixels that are neither transparent nor one of the flat colours the file declares — the anti-aliased ones — were counted, as a share of the mark's own painted area: 24px 29.7% · 36px 26.6% · 48px 18.3% · 60px 18.3% 72px 14.5% · 96px 12.5% — each one a local minimum 40px 29.9% · 56px 25.7% · 64px 21.7% — each beaten by a neighbour Two corrections came out of that and both are in the numbers above. The share is only comparable BETWEEN NEIGHBOURS: a small mark has more edge per unit of area, so 24 reads worse than 96 for a reason that has nothing to do with the grid, and 36 actually renders cleaner than 24. And the local minima are every multiple of TWELVE, not only of 24 — 36 and 60 qualify. The union stays on the multiples of 24 because they are the strongest tier on both measures and the only ones also on the 8-point grid, but 36 and 60 are legitimate if a frame ever needs them, and `check:logo-grid` will pass them. WHAT THIS COSTS, and it is worth saying plainly: 16 and 32 are on the 8-point grid and are NOT on this list, because one 96-unit drawing cannot be crisp at them — 5.7% each. A mark that must be sharp at 16 or 32 needs its own drawing at that size, which is what optical sizing is for and what Material and SF Symbols both ship. That is artwork work, not a prop. 56 AND 64 WERE REMOVED 2026-08-24. Both were added for one frame each — 56 for the product mega-menu row (`FlyoutMenu-product`, Figma `1014:1921`, where the instance measures 56.000003814697266, i.e. dragged rather than chosen) and 64 for the iron-homepage changelog tiles (`2418:8806`). Neither is a local maximum: 56 draws 3.4% where 48 next door draws 18.9%, and 64 draws 5.7% where 72 draws 11.4%. A union that grows by one frame at a time stops being a list of sizes that render well and becomes a list of sizes someone needed, which is what `height` already is for the non-square kinds. THE ELEMENT ROW MOVED UNDER THIS COMMENT ONCE. Until 2026-08-24 it read a flat 0.3% at every size, with the conclusion that the grid rule is meaningless for the elements. That was TRUE when written (`1a6cff6`) and false three commits later: `91cd864` re-exported all ten off their pre-ramp colours and re-drew their paths. They are now on THIRDS rather than eighths, which is why their column peaks at 96/192 (12.6%) instead of tracking the marks. Two families, two grids — the ladder follows the MARK, where the difference is visible, and the elements are along for the ride until they are re-exported onto eighths. 32 WAS ASKED FOR ON 2026-08-31, by a consuming room that needed it for the product element — Figma `2407:12727` draws that element at 32 ten times. The paragraph above already answered it for the MARK (5.7%, and a mark that must be sharp at 32 needs its own drawing). What that paragraph did not say, because it treats the elements as along for the ride, is that 32 IS a local maximum for the ELEMENTS: 2.8% against 24's 2.1%. So the request was right about its own family and still cannot be granted — `size` is one union across both, a size has to be a local maximum in both, and for the marks 32 is beaten by 24 by exactly the 2x factor the rule uses. Adding it would turn `check:logo-grid` red. Swept 8-96 with `node scripts/check-logo-grid.mjs --probe`, the two families agree everywhere except FOUR sizes, and they are worth naming because the next request will be one of them: 32 element only 64 element only 36 mark only 60 mark only Both families are local maxima at 8, 12, 24, 48, 72 and 96 — the multiples of 12 — and the union is that agreement from 24 up. Which is also why 64 keeps coming back: like 32 it is a real step on the element ladder and a trough on the mark's. The way to serve either is artwork or a split prop, not a wider union. `check:logo-grid` derives all of this from the SVGs on every run: the table above is compared to a fresh count, and every member of the union has to be a local maximum. Re-export the artwork and the gate re-derives the ladder rather than believing this paragraph. Off-grid edges are visible on a hairline and these marks have none — they are solid colour blocks. Still: reach for a ladder size anywhere one will do, because the mark is where the difference is real.

props.name: height
props.description: kind="wordmark" / "lockup" — rendered height in px; width follows the aspect ratio.

props.name: href
props.description: Wraps the logo in an <a>.

props.name: label
props.description: Overrides the generated alt text. Pass "" for decorative use next to a visible name.

props.name: live
props.description: Whether the notice announces itself to a screen reader. Default: `true` for a notice that appeared in response to something the user did, which is what the intents describe. Pass `false` when the notice is static page furniture — a live region that is already on screen at load can be announced out of nowhere, which is worse than saying nothing.

props.name: size
props.description: `lg` 56px (16/700 label) · `md` 48px (14/600). Figma draws only these two.

props.name: subtext
props.description: The install count under the label. Figma carries a `hasDownloadCount` boolean beside the string; here the string's presence IS the switch, since unlike TextLink's `external` the layer being toggled has content of its own and there is nothing to show without it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: The trailing caret. Figma's `hasTrailingIcon`, and a real axis: it is off wherever the button does not open anything.

props.name: product
props.description: Mark artwork — same keys as Logo.astro's `product`.

props.name: productName
props.description: Coloured half of the wordmark, e.g. "PDF" in IRONPDF.

props.name: runtime
props.description: Trailing runtime label, e.g. "for .NET". Omit to hide.

props.name: hasTrailingIcon
props.description: Figma `hasTrailingIcon` — the caret after the product lockup.

props.name: subLead
props.description: Sub tier: the current-page chip, drawn boxed. Figma keeps its label the default colour and turns it brand-pink only on hover.

props.name: showMenuItems2
props.description: Figma `showMenuItems2` — trailing links at the right end of the sub tier.

props.name: cta
props.description: Which component fills the CTA slot. Figma models this as an INSTANCE-SWAP property called `Instance` on `790:4778`, whose preferred list is exactly two: `button-Nuget` and `button` pinned at `231:1411` (`Variant=primary, Size=md`). A closed set of two is a prop here rather than a slot — it is an enum on the canvas, this repo does not spell a variant axis as a boolean or an open hole, and a prop is the only one of the two that `check:props-table` and the manifest can see. BOTH VALUES ARE 48 TALL AND THAT IS THE WHOLE CONSTRAINT. `314:205` is 368 x 48.0004 inside a 72 tier — 12 + 48 + 12 — so the swap is safe only at `size=md`. `button` at lg is 56 and would make the tier 80; that is why the preferred instance is pinned to a VARIANT and not to the `231:1406` set, and why `size` is fixed here rather than exposed. The `cta` band below measures both values so a future edit cannot quietly reintroduce it.

props.name: labelSize
props.description: Label typography ramp. 'md' (default) is the 14px form label; 'sm' is the 12px caption.

props.name: rows
props.description: Height in text rows. **Omit it** and the box is Figma's own 98px — a designed number, not three lines of 28 plus padding, which is what `rows` would give. Passing `rows` hands the height back to the browser.

props.name: variant
props.description: Figma's `Variant`. `action` left-aligns the bubble and opens the title's icon slot; `default` centres everything. A tooltip carrying a link is `action` whether or not you say so — Figma draws no centred tooltip with a link, and that inference is what the component did before the prop existed.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading glyph in the title, by name from `../icons`. Figma draws `buildings`; any icon in the set works. Needs a `title` to sit in, and is ignored on the `default` variant, which Figma draws without one.

props.name: wide
props.description: Widens the bubble to a fixed 350px for long copy. Was `maxWidth` until 2026-08-06 — a boolean named like a length, setting `width`, not `max-width`.

props.name: variant
props.description: Figma's `variant` — `transparent` is Figma's "Without bg".

props.name: showAddress
props.description: Figma's `showAddress` toggle.

props.name: address
props.default: '205 N. Michigan Ave. Chicago, IL 60611, USA'

props.name: inputLabel
props.description: The field's real label. The card's design has no room for a visible one, so it is rendered visually hidden rather than left out — a placeholder is not a label: it is not announced by every screen reader, and it disappears the moment the user types, taking the only description of the field with it. Defaults to the placeholder text.

$internalComment: Not exported by name and not counted above: rendered by the public components, reachable via the package's ./internal/* export. Described here so gates and tooling can see them; a consumer should not import them.

props.name: label
props.description: Trigger label.

props.name: openOnHover
props.description: Opens on hover as well as on click/focus. Off by default: on touch there is no hover to leave, and the pattern is only ever an enhancement.

props.name: open
props.description: Render open on first paint — for docs and tests, not for a live nav.

props.name: align
props.description: Which edge the panel is pinned to. A wide mega-menu under a trigger near the right of the bar has to hang left or it leaves the viewport; `center` is the ironsoftware.com arrangement, where the panel is much wider than its trigger.

props.name: notch
props.description: Draws the notch pointing up at the trigger.

props.name: bare
props.description: Drop the panel's own surface — background, border, radius, shadow and the inner padding — because the content brings its own. `ProductFlyout` does: it is a card in its own right, and stacking the two put a 12px radius and a modal shadow around a 12px radius and a modal shadow. The notch is NOT dropped. It belongs to the flyout, not to the content — it points at the trigger, which the content knows nothing about.

props.name: logoSrc
props.description: Already-encoded path to the 22px mark that fades in on hover.

props.name: class
props.description: Lands on the <li>. The docs page uses it to force the hover illustration — `.demo-row-hover img` and `.demo-row-hover .text-text-dark-support` — since :hover cannot be rendered statically. Footer itself passes nothing.

props.name: suite
props.description: The left rail. Omit to render the columns alone.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Bold half of the lockup wordmark.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Coloured half.

props.name: donateLabel
props.description: Text beside the 1%-for-the-Planet mark.

props.name: basePath
props.description: Where `docs/assets/` was copied to — same escape hatch as `Logo`.

props.name: forceHover
props.description: Renders the rail and the first product in their hover state, for the docs page. `:hover` cannot be captured statically, and the two halves hover independently, so this forces both at once for one illustration.
